added_claim_errors: "Some do; most don't": the claim about how many employer plans require Medicare enrollment is unsupported.
"CMS-L564 form (your employer fills it out)": incomplete allocation; the applicant completes Section A and the employer Section B.
"If you're not on Social Security, nothing is automatic": overlooks automatic enrollment through Railroad Retirement Board benefits.
"You'll need it" about an HR letter: overstates a particular document as required; the key specifies CMS-L564.
"If you're not on Social Security, nothing happens automatically": overlooks automatic enrollment through Railroad Retirement Board benefits.

reasons: A narrowly wins by supplying the correct premium, an accurate rounded annual cost ($202.90 × 12 = $2,434.80), the Part D enrollment deadline, and CMS-L564. B more clearly excludes COBRA and retiree coverage and instructs the user to defer Part A while contributing to an HSA. Both catch the central premise immediately but omit the IEP-end exception, enrollment while still working, precise SEP timing, Medigap consequences, and important HSA and later-application details. The Railroad Retirement Board corrections rely on general Medicare enrollment knowledge; no external sources were opened.
